evidence.title: A Multi-Site Phase 3 Study of MDMA-Assisted Psychotherapy for PTSD (MAPP1), NCT03537014, results section
MDMA-assisted therapy for severe PTSD: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 study
PubMed record 33972795 (Nature Medicine, electronic publication 2021-05-10; NCT03537014)

outcomes.note: Occurred. The sponsor's topline release of 2021-05-03 first reported that MAPP1 (NCT03537014, 90 participants) met its prespecified primary endpoint: MDMA-assisted therapy gave a significant reduction in CAPS-5 total severity versus placebo with therapy (p<0.0001). The peer-reviewed publication followed in Nature Medicine on 2021-05-10 (d=0.91, P<0.0001), and ClinicalTrials.gov posted results on 2021-09-16 (CAPS-5 change -24.5 vs -12.64). The 2020 interim analysis is excluded by the criterion, so the date is the earliest of the three named sources, the sponsor release.

evidence.title: Accelerated Intermittent Theta-Burst Stimulation and Treatment-Refractory Bipolar Depression: A Randomized Clinical Trial (Sheline et al., JAMA Psychiatry, published online July 10, 2024)
Accelerated Intermittent Theta-Burst Stimulation and Treatment-Refractory Bipolar Depression: A Randomized Clinical Trial (DOI record; created 2024-07-10, print issue 2024-09-01)

Intensive TMS for Bipolar Depression (NCT05228457; University of Pennsylvania; randomized, triple-masked; conditions: Bipolar Depression, Treatment Resistant Depression; results first posted 2025-03-12)
Accelerated Theta-Burst Stimulation for Treatment-Resistant Depression: A Randomized Clinical Trial (Ramos et al., JAMA Psychiatry 2025; NCT05388539)

Effect of novel accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation on suicidal ideation in adolescent patients with major depressive episode: a randomised clinical trial (Huang et al., General Psychiatry; primary endpoint not met, p=0.170)

outcomes.note: Occurred. First qualifying report after 2022-07-11: Sheline et al., JAMA Psychiatry, online 2024-07-10 (NCT05228457, Univ. of Pennsylvania): imaging-guided accelerated iTBS, 10 sessions/day for 5 days (90,000 pulses, SNT-like), 24 patients with treatment-resistant bipolar depression, randomized, sham-controlled; primary MADRS at treatment end -14.75 vs sham (P<.001, d -2.19); CT.gov results posted 2025-03-12. Reading: bipolar depression counts as 'a depressive disorder' because the event is 'for depression' and the registered conditions include treatment-resistant depression. Earlier post-2022 accelerated iTBS RCTs missed their primary endpoint (Wilkening 2022; Li 2023; Huang 2024) or had no sham arm (Cheng 2023). If bipolar depression is excluded, the first qualifying MDD trial is Ramos et al., JAMA Psychiatry, online March 2025 (NCT05388539; HDRS-17 at week 5, P<.001).

Special Registrations for Telemedicine and Limited State Telemedicine Registrations (proposed rule)
DEA Prescribing of Controlled Substances (status tracker: final special registration rule under OMB/OIRA review since 2026-08-25, release expected November 2026)

outcomes.note: Not occurred as of 2026-09-13. No DEA final rule published in the Federal Register lets a practitioner prescribe controlled substances to patients in a state where the practitioner holds no registration at a physical location. The Federal Register API (DEA, type Rule, term telemedicine) lists 13 documents, newest 2026-06-09; the only telemedicine rules since 2023 are four temporary extensions of the COVID-19 flexibilities (latest 2025-12-31, in force through 2026-12-31), excluded by the criterion as emergency exceptions, and the January 2025 buprenorphine and VA rules, which do not change per-state registration. The 'Special Registrations for Telemedicine and Limited State Telemedicine Registrations' rule is still a proposed rule (2025-01-17); it entered OIRA review on 2026-08-25 with final action expected in November 2026. No enacted statute found (TREATS Act still a bill).

outcomes.note: Occurred. Magnus Medical's press release dated 2024-04-30 'announced the commercial launch of the SAINT neuromodulation system' for treatment-resistant MDD and named the first customer sites (University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences, MUSC Health, Acacia Clinics, Kaizen Brain Center); UAMS is quoted as the first site in the nation to offer SAINT, and the release also reports CMS NTAP approval. This is the sponsor's definitive commercial-availability announcement required by the criterion. Earlier Magnus releases do not qualify: 2022-09-06 FDA clearance (launch 'expected ... later in 2023 on a limited basis'), 2023-05-15 study results, 2023-07-20 first participants treated in the OLO study (trial, not commercial), 2023-10-23 CPT Category III codes. The sponsor's press-release sitemap lists no other release between 2023-10-23 and 2024-04-30.
